engine.meaning: Mostly the original verbatim, but the last answer is changed: "Does Yellowstone include a federally designated bush?" and "Parliament House hasn't acted on the recommendation" swap wilderness for bush and Congress for an Australian building.
engine.sense: Several wrong-sense swaps: "federally designated bush" (a legal wilderness category is not "bush"), "Parliament House" for Congress, "Not on your nelly" for a plain "No." "summer is flat chat" strains for "busy".
engine.authenticity: Stock tokens dropped into American prose: "before you lob", "Nah, nah.", "Not on your nelly."; "purchasing your pass" and "lines at the entrance gates" left in.
engine.register: Largely untranslated, with a handful of swapped words ("make a booking early", "visitor centres"); far under level 4.
engine.tone: The friendly informational tone mostly survives because the text is mostly untouched, but "Not on your nelly." makes a factual answer flippant.
engine.flow: Reads like the original except where words are swapped in: "Be sure to make a booking early!" under "Do I need a reservation", "before you lob" mid-formal sentence.
engine.variety: Too little Aussie to vary; "Nah, nah." and "Not on your nelly." are the only touches beyond spellings.
engine.essence: Still the Yellowstone FAQ, unchanged for most of its length, but the last answer no longer makes sense.

yarn-troppo.meaning: Every fact survives, with colour hung off the original: "anywhere a bison's wandered up to the road and every car's pulled over for a squiz", "Lewis and Clark had a bob each way", "Pipped at the post." "look but don't touch" overstates "unimpaired", and "Only the northern half" shifts "part".
yarn-troppo.sense: Terms fit: "had a bob each way" for using both names, "the whole box and dice", "Not a bad gong, that." for the UN designation, "the pollies in Congress". "look but don't touch" strains for a preservation mandate.
yarn-troppo.authenticity: Sounds like a real Australian guide: "Do yourself a favour", "you'll skip a fair bit of mucking about", "Now, this one's a ripper."
yarn-troppo.register: A full level-4 retelling; no swearing, which vulgarity 1 allows.
yarn-troppo.tone: Keeps the FAQ's friendly, helpful tone while chattier: "Please be patient and enjoy your visit. It's worth the wait, I reckon." "dangerously cold" is kept straight.
yarn-troppo.flow: Reads aloud smoothly: "After that, folks just kept saying it till it was official".
yarn-troppo.variety: Varied slang and openers ("lob", "flat chat", "squiz", "box and dice", "gong", "pollies"); "get this" comes twice ("So get this", "And get this") and "squiz" twice.
yarn-troppo.essence: Unmistakably the Yellowstone FAQ, question by question, retold as a guide's chat.

unharnessed.meaning: All facts survive. Additions are colour: "cold enough to freeze the bits off a brass monkey", "have a ripper of a visit".
unharnessed.sense: Terms fit: "rock up", "flat out", "gawk at the wildlife", "track maintenance", "bloody competitive". "have a ripper of a visit" is a slight strain.
unharnessed.authenticity: Natural: "Congress still hasn't got round to doing anything about it", "kick off their careers". The brass-monkey line is stock.
unharnessed.register: About level 3 to 4: much is plain Australian English ("Ask at the visitor centres about what's been spotted lately"), with one "bloody", within vulgarity 1.
unharnessed.tone: Friendly and informative; the brass-monkey joke lightens a safety warning slightly ("dangerously cold – cold enough to freeze the bits off a brass monkey").
unharnessed.flow: Smooth throughout: "Over time the name got locked in"
unharnessed.variety: Varied enough ("rock up", "gawk", "heaps", "kick off", "bloody") with no tics.
unharnessed.essence: Clearly the FAQ, retold in an Australian voice.

dinkum-3.meaning: Every fact survives; it adds accurate metric conversions ("13 million acres, or about 5.3 million hectares", "11,358 feet (3,462 metres)"), a localisation rather than a change. "the number of people coming for a bit of fun outdoors" loosens "recreational visitors".
dinkum-3.sense: Mostly exact ("lob", "flat chat", "have a geek", "dead competitive"), but "book your car in" reads as booking a car service, and "the lower 48" is a US term.
dinkum-3.authenticity: Natural Australian voice: "That'd be Eagle Peak", "Best not: swimming isn't recommended", "Pop into a visitor centre". "the lower 48 of the United States" is American.
dinkum-3.register: Close to level 4, Aussie throughout but measured; no swearing.
dinkum-3.tone: Friendly and helpful throughout, warnings kept straight: "Best not: swimming isn't recommended".
dinkum-3.flow: Mostly smooth; the run of hectare brackets in one answer is a little heavy ("(at 2.2 million acres, or about 890,000 hectares)").
dinkum-3.essence: Unmistakably the FAQ, retold for an Australian reader down to the metric units.

yarn-dinkum.meaning: Every fact survives with almost no additions: "Over time the name stuck, official-like".
yarn-dinkum.sense: All terms fit: "before you lob", "flat chat", "roadworks", "hotly contested", "Yeah, nah."
yarn-dinkum.authenticity: Natural where it changes things ("Get your booking in early!"); "official-like" is a little stagey.
yarn-dinkum.register: Light: level 2 to 3, many answers near the original ("Park rangers work in education, resource management, law enforcement").
yarn-dinkum.tone: The friendly informational tone is whole: "Please be patient and enjoy your visit."
yarn-dinkum.variety: Little slang to vary; "Nah, nah." and "Yeah, nah." plus "lob" and "flat chat".

engine.quote: Does Yellowstone include a federally designated bush?
engine.original: Does Yellowstone include a federally designated wilderness?
engine.why: "Wilderness" is a legal designation; "bush" makes the question meaningless.

engine.quote: Parliament House hasn't acted on the recommendation
engine.original: Congress has not acted on the recommendation
engine.why: Moves a US federal decision to the Australian Parliament.
Emphatic refusal idiom for a factual no; wrong register.
"Flat chat" fits people being busy, strains for a season.

summaries.engine: A rule-engine pass: barely translated, and its two big swaps (bush, Parliament House) break the last answer.
summaries.yarn-troppo: A lively, natural level-4 retelling that keeps every fact; the best of the set.
summaries.unharnessed: Clean, natural and faithful, a little lighter than level 4, with one jokey line on a warning.
summaries.dinkum-3: Natural and faithful, thoughtfully localised with metric units; a little short of B's life.
summaries.yarn-dinkum: Faithful and natural but lighter than level 4.
